title: Doxorubicin inhibits SIRT2 and NF-kB p65 phosphorylation in Brest cell-line cancer.
authors: Rezgui, Abdelmalek; Tachour, Rechda Amel; Layaida, Houdhaifa; Derguine, Rania; Hab, Fatma Zahra; Benmanseur, Anfel; Matougui, Brahim; Agred, Rym; Sobhi, Widad
one_liner_zh: 该文研究阿霉素抑制SIRT2和NF-kB p65磷酸化诱导乳腺癌细胞凋亡，虽含分子对接但核心是药物-蛋白互作，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合机制，与本课题关联弱。
abstract: Doxorubicin (DOXO) is a widely used anti-cancer agent, yet the precise mechanism underlying the induction of tumor cell death remains unclear. This study aimed to elucidate new mechanisms by which doxorubicin induces apoptosis in the EMT6 mouse breast carcinoma cell line. The role of doxorubicin was assessed using the XTT assay. The assessment of oxidative stress markers, alongside the analysis of SIRT2 and NF-kappaB p65 (RelA) phosphorylation inhibition, was conducted. In silico studies, including density functional theory (DFT) calculations and molecular docking simulations, were employed to characterize the molecular interactions between doxorubicin and SIRT2. Additionally, doxorubicin was assessed for its capacity to modulate gene expression and associated pathways using multiple bioinformatics tools and web-based platforms. Our finding indicates that Doxorubicin induced apoptosis in EMT6 cells with an IC50 of 8,32 muM. At lower concentrations, doxorubicin enhances the oxidative balance and promotes cell viability. At high concentrations, doxorubicin inhibits SIRT2. Furthermore, an experimental investigation revealed that doxorubicin inhibits RelA phosphorylation. The results also showed that doxorubicin modulated the expression of 19 genes involved in different pathways and several transcription factors. The results of implementing the gene set with SIRT2 and RELA consolidated the experimental results. In conclusion, Doxorubicin was observed to induce EMT6 apoptosis through the inhibition of SIRT2 and RelA proteins. The outcomes of both experimental and bioinformatic studies provide a novel perspective on the biological effects of doxorubicin and underscore the potential of inhibiting the SIRT2-RelA axis as a promising biological target for cancer therapy.
abstract_zh: 阿霉素（DOXO）是一种广泛使用的抗癌药物，但其诱导肿瘤细胞死亡的精确机制仍不清楚。本研究旨在阐明阿霉素在EMT6小鼠乳腺癌细胞系中诱导凋亡的新机制。使用XTT实验评估了阿霉素的作用。进行了氧化应激标志物的评估，同时分析了SIRT2和NF-kappaB p65（RelA）磷酸化的抑制作用。采用计算机模拟研究，包括密度泛函理论（DFT）计算和分子对接模拟，以表征阿霉素与SIRT2之间的分子相互作用。此外，利用多种生物信息学工具和基于网络的平台评估了阿霉素调节基因表达及相关通路的能力。我们的发现表明，阿霉素以8.32 μM的IC50诱导EMT6细胞凋亡。在较低浓度下，阿霉素增强氧化平衡并促进细胞活力。在高浓度下，阿霉素抑制SIRT2。此外，实验研究显示，阿霉素抑制RelA磷酸化。结果还表明，阿霉素调节了涉及不同通路和多个转录因子的19个基因的表达。将基因集与SIRT2和RELA结合实施的结果巩固了实验结果。总之，观察到阿霉素通过抑制SIRT2和RelA蛋白诱导EMT6凋亡。实验和生物信息学研究的结果为阿霉素的生物学效应提供了新视角，并强调了抑制SIRT2-RelA轴作为癌症治疗有前景的生物学靶点的潜力。
